input.content:
# Benchmark Profile Signal Quality: Before/After Comparison

This document shows how replacing go-git `wt.Add()`/`wt.Commit()` with git CLI
in benchmark setup code improved pprof profile signal, making it possible to
identify actual CLI code bottlenecks.

**Commits:**
- Before: `7ee7d8ba` (benchmark infrastructure with go-git setup)
- After: `e418a1c0` (benchmark setup uses git CLI subprocesses)

**Why this matters:** Go's pprof captures all in-process CPU/memory, including
benchmark setup. `b.StopTimer()` only excludes setup from wall-clock measurement,
not from profiles. By moving setup to git CLI subprocesses, pprof now only sees
the code we're actually benchmarking.

---

## Strategy Package (SaveStep, PostCommit, PrepareCommitMsg, GetRewindPoints)

These are the most performance-critical benchmarks — they measure the hooks and
checkpoint operations that run on every agent interaction and every commit.

### CPU Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total samples** | **18.95s** | **8.50s** (-55%) |

**Before — Top entries are benchmark setup noise:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 54.7% | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 51.6% | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` | 30.9% | Setup + real |
| 4 | `strategy.benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` | 27.3% | Setup |
| 5 | `go-git Worktree.Status` | 26.3% | Setup |

**After — Top entries are actual CLI code paths:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.WriteTemporary`** | 40.7% | **Measured code** |
| 2 | `benchutil.BenchRepo.SeedShadowBranch` | 40.0% | Setup (real checkpoint code) |
| 3 | `go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` | 34.9% | Real (blob writes) |
| 4 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.buildTreeWithChanges`** | 34.2% | **Measured code** |
| 5 | `go-git ObjectWriter.Close` | 23.4% | Real (object persistence) |

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total allocations** | **4,711 MB** | **1,111 MB** (-76%) |

**Before — 78% of allocations are from benchmark setup:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 3,712 MB (78.8%) | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 3,666 MB (77.8%) | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git Worktree.Status` | 2,503 MB (53.1%) | Setup |
| 4 | `go-git Worktree.status` | 2,431 MB (51.6%) | Setup |
| 5 | `strategy.benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` | 2,067 MB (43.9%) | Setup |

**After — Top allocators are actual checkpoint code:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.WriteTemporary`** | 602 MB (54.2%) | **Measured code** |
| 2 | `benchutil.BenchRepo.SeedShadowBranch` | 594 MB (53.4%) | Setup (real checkpoint code) |
| 3 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.buildTreeWithChanges`** | 520 MB (46.8%) | **Measured code** |
| 4 | `go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` | 417 MB (37.6%) | Real (blob writes) |
| 5 | `go-git osfs.BoundOS.abs` | 330 MB (29.7%) | Real (path resolution) |

### Bottlenecks now visible in strategy profiles

With setup noise removed, the profiles reveal actionable optimization targets:

1. **`checkpoint.GitStore.buildTreeWithChanges`** (34% CPU, 47% mem) — Tree surgery
   for each checkpoint. Uses `ApplyTreeChanges` which walks affected subtrees.
2. **`go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject`** (35% CPU, 38% mem) — Writing blobs
   and trees to `.git/objects/`. Each object is zlib-compressed individually.
3. **`go-git osfs.BoundOS.abs` → `SecureJoinVFS`** (30% mem) — Path validation
   on every filesystem operation. go-git calls `filepath-securejoin` per object write.
4. **`go-git ObjectWriter.Close/save`** (23% CPU, 27% mem) — Flushing compressed
   objects to disk with fsync.

---

## Commands Package (Status, Enable)

### CPU Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total samples** | **950ms** | **580ms** (-39%) |

**Before — Setup dominates even this small package:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 45.3% | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 35.8% | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git Worktree.copyFileToStorage` | 24.2% | Setup |

**After — Actual command code visible:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | `os.RemoveAll` | 31.0% | Cleanup (test teardown) |
| 2 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 17.2% | Setup (reduced) |
| 3 | No go-git Worktree entries | — | Eliminated |

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total allocations** | **145.86 MB** | **47.14 MB** (-68%) |

**Before — 83% is setup:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 121 MB (83.1%) | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 101 MB (69.1%) | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git Worktree.doAddFile` | 63 MB (43.0%) | Setup |
| 4 | `compress/flate.NewWriter` | 41 MB (28.0%) | Setup |

**After — Enable command code path now visible:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 13.9 MB (29.4%) | Setup (reduced) |
| 2 | **`cli.setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`** | 10.7 MB (22.8%) | **Measured code** |
| 3 | **`strategy.EnsureSetup`** | 9.2 MB (19.5%) | **Measured code** |
| 4 | **`strategy.EnsureMetadataBranch`** | 8.7 MB (18.5%) | **Measured code** |

### Bottlenecks now visible in commands profiles

1. **`setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`** (23% mem) — The enable command's hook
   installation path. Previously invisible under setup noise.
2. **`strategy.EnsureMetadataBranch`** (19% mem) — Creating/verifying the
   `entire/checkpoints/v1` orphan branch. Allocates ~8.7 MB per invocation.

---

## Tree Operations Package (UpdateSubtree, ApplyTreeChanges, WriteTemporary, WriteCommitted)

Tree benchmarks test go-git plumbing operations directly. The setup
(`buildShardedMetadataTree`, `buildFlatFileTree`) also uses go-git, so the
before/after difference is smaller here — both are measuring go-git code.

### CPU Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total samples** | **27.76s** | **24.95s** (-10%) |

Top entries are nearly identical because the benchmarks themselves use go-git:

| Rank | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| 1 | `ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` (60%) | `ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` (62%) |
| 2 | `checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent` (31%) | `checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent` (34%) |
| 3 | `buildShardedMetadataTree` (28%) | `buildShardedMetadataTree` (31%) |

The ~10% reduction comes from `NewBenchRepo` no longer using go-git for its
initial commit (only affects `BenchmarkWriteTemporary` and `BenchmarkSeedShadowBranch`).

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total allocations** | **4,493 MB** | **3,698 MB** (-18%) |

**Before — `NewBenchRepo` setup mixed with real benchmark code:**

Top entries are all go-git internals — hard to distinguish setup from measured code.

**After — `NewBenchRepo` reduced, real code more prominent:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.WriteCommitted`** | 1,341 MB (36.3%) | **Measured code** |
| 2 | **`checkpoint.writeStandardCheckpointEntries`** | 1,159 MB (31.3%) | **Measured code** |
| 3 | **`checkpoint.writeSessionToSubdirectory`** | 1,128 MB (30.5%) | **Measured code** |
| 4 | **`checkpoint.writeTranscript`** | 1,088 MB (29.4%) | **Measured code** |
| 5 | **`checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent`** | 1,068 MB (28.9%) | **Measured code** |

### Bottlenecks now visible in tree profiles

1. **`checkpoint.writeTranscript`** (29% mem) — Serializing transcript data to
   git blobs. Largest single allocation source in `WriteCommitted`.
2. **`checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent`** (29% mem) — Creating individual git
   blob objects. Each call allocates zlib writer + buffer.
3. **`SecureJoinVFS`** (29% mem) — Path security validation on every go-git
   filesystem operation. Significant cumulative cost.

---

## Summary

| Package | Profile Type | Before (setup noise) | After (clean signal) | Reduction |
|---------|-------------|---------------------|---------------------|-----------|
| **Strategy** | CPU samples | 18.95s | 8.50s | **-55%** |
| **Strategy** | Memory | 4,711 MB | 1,111 MB | **-76%** |
| **Commands** | CPU samples | 950ms | 580ms | **-39%** |
| **Commands** | Memory | 146 MB | 47 MB | **-68%** |
| **Tree ops** | CPU samples | 27.76s | 24.95s | **-10%** |
| **Tree ops** | Memory | 4,493 MB | 3,698 MB | **-18%** |

The largest improvements are in the **strategy** and **commands** packages where
`NewBenchRepo`'s go-git `wt.Add()` was the dominant allocator. The tree ops package
shows smaller improvement because its benchmarks inherently use go-git plumbing.

**Key insight:** Before the fix, the top 5 pprof entries across all packages were
go-git's `Worktree.Add`, `Worktree.Status`, and `NewBenchRepo` — none of which are
actual CLI code. After the fix, the top entries are `WriteTemporary`,
`buildTreeWithChanges`, `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`, and `EnsureMetadataBranch`
— all real CLI code paths where optimization effort would yield user-visible improvements.

content.text:
The current PNGs are **per-package** aggregates — each PNG contains all benchmarks from that package combined into one profile. That means:

- `strategy_cpu.png` mixes **existing** (PostCommit, PrepareCommitMsg, GetStagedFiles) with **new** (SaveStep, GetRewindPoints)
- `commands_cpu.png` is **all existing** (Enable, Status)
- `tree_cpu.png` is **all existing** (WriteTemporary, UpdateSubtree, etc.)

There's no way to split pprof profiles per-benchmark after the fact — Go's `-cpuprofile` captures the entire test binary. To get separate images for existing vs new benchmarks, I'd need to run them separately using `-bench` filters.

input.command:
# Get before/after memory totals for each benchmark to find the best improvement
echo "=== Per-Benchmark Memory Profile Totals ==="
echo ""
printf "%-25s %-8s %12s %12s %8s\n" "Benchmark" "Label" "Before(MB)" "After(MB)" "Change"
echo "$(printf '%.0s-' {1..75})"

while IFS='|' read -r pkg filter name label; do
  before_total=$(go tool pprof -top "bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/${name}_mem.prof" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9.]+MB total' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9.]+')
  after_total=$(go tool pprof -top "bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/${name}_mem.prof" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '[0-9.]+MB total' | head -1 | grep -oE '[0-9.]+')
  
  if [ -n "$before_total" ] && [ -n "$after_total" ]; then
    # Calculate percentage change using awk
    change=$(awk "BEGIN {printf \"%.0f\", (($after_total - $before_total) / $before_total) * 100}")
    printf "%-25s %-8s %10sMB %10sMB %7s%%\n" "$name" "[$label]" "$before_total" "$after_total" "$change"
  else
    printf "%-25s %-8s %12s %12s %8s\n" "$name" "[$label]" "${before_total:-n/a}" "${after_total:-n/a}" "—"
  fi
done < /tmp/bench_list.txt

  if [ -n "$before_total" ] && [ -n "$after_total" ]; then
    change=$(awk "BEGIN {printf \"%.0f\", (($after_total - $before_total) / $before_total) * 100}")
    printf "%-25s %-8s %10ss %10ss %7s%%\n" "$name" "[$label]" "$before_total" "$after_total" "$change"
  else
    printf "%-25s %-8s %12s %12s %8s\n" "$name" "[$label]" "${before_total:-n/a}" "${after_total:-n/a}" "—"
  fi
done < /tmp/bench_list.txt

# Benchmark Profile Signal Quality: Before/After Comparison

This document shows how replacing go-git `wt.Add()`/`wt.Commit()` with git CLI
in benchmark setup code improved pprof profile signal, making it possible to
identify actual CLI code bottlenecks.

**Commits:**
- Before: `7ee7d8ba` (benchmark infrastructure with go-git setup)
- After: `e418a1c0` (benchmark setup uses git CLI subprocesses)

**Why this matters:** Go's pprof captures all in-process CPU/memory, including
benchmark setup. `b.StopTimer()` only excludes setup from wall-clock measurement,
not from profiles. By moving setup to git CLI subprocesses, pprof now only sees
the code we're actually benchmarking.

---

## Strategy Package (SaveStep, PostCommit, PrepareCommitMsg, GetRewindPoints)

These are the most performance-critical benchmarks — they measure the hooks and
checkpoint operations that run on every agent interaction and every commit.

### CPU Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total samples** | **18.95s** | **8.50s** (-55%) |

**Before — Top entries are benchmark setup noise:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 54.7% | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 51.6% | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` | 30.9% | Setup + real |
| 4 | `strategy.benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` | 27.3% | Setup |
| 5 | `go-git Worktree.Status` | 26.3% | Setup |

**After — Top entries are actual CLI code paths:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.WriteTemporary`** | 40.7% | **Measured code** |
| 2 | `benchutil.BenchRepo.SeedShadowBranch` | 40.0% | Setup (real checkpoint code) |
| 3 | `go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` | 34.9% | Real (blob writes) |
| 4 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.buildTreeWithChanges`** | 34.2% | **Measured code** |
| 5 | `go-git ObjectWriter.Close` | 23.4% | Real (object persistence) |

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total allocations** | **4,711 MB** | **1,111 MB** (-76%) |

**Before — 78% of allocations are from benchmark setup:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 3,712 MB (78.8%) | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 3,666 MB (77.8%) | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git Worktree.Status` | 2,503 MB (53.1%) | Setup |
| 4 | `go-git Worktree.status` | 2,431 MB (51.6%) | Setup |
| 5 | `strategy.benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` | 2,067 MB (43.9%) | Setup |

**After — Top allocators are actual checkpoint code:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.WriteTemporary`** | 602 MB (54.2%) | **Measured code** |
| 2 | `benchutil.BenchRepo.SeedShadowBranch` | 594 MB (53.4%) | Setup (real checkpoint code) |
| 3 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.buildTreeWithChanges`** | 520 MB (46.8%) | **Measured code** |
| 4 | `go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` | 417 MB (37.6%) | Real (blob writes) |
| 5 | `go-git osfs.BoundOS.abs` | 330 MB (29.7%) | Real (path resolution) |

### Bottlenecks now visible in strategy profiles

With setup noise removed, the profiles reveal actionable optimization targets:

1. **`checkpoint.GitStore.buildTreeWithChanges`** (34% CPU, 47% mem) — Tree surgery
   for each checkpoint. Uses `ApplyTreeChanges` which walks affected subtrees.
2. **`go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject`** (35% CPU, 38% mem) — Writing blobs
   and trees to `.git/objects/`. Each object is zlib-compressed individually.
3. **`go-git osfs.BoundOS.abs` → `SecureJoinVFS`** (30% mem) — Path validation
   on every filesystem operation. go-git calls `filepath-securejoin` per object write.
4. **`go-git ObjectWriter.Close/save`** (23% CPU, 27% mem) — Flushing compressed
   objects to disk with fsync.

---

## Commands Package (Status, Enable)

### CPU Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total samples** | **950ms** | **580ms** (-39%) |

**Before — Setup dominates even this small package:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 45.3% | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 35.8% | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git Worktree.copyFileToStorage` | 24.2% | Setup |

**After — Actual command code visible:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | `os.RemoveAll` | 31.0% | Cleanup (test teardown) |
| 2 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 17.2% | Setup (reduced) |
| 3 | No go-git Worktree entries | — | Eliminated |

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total allocations** | **145.86 MB** | **47.14 MB** (-68%) |

**Before — 83% is setup:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 121 MB (83.1%) | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 101 MB (69.1%) | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git Worktree.doAddFile` | 63 MB (43.0%) | Setup |
| 4 | `compress/flate.NewWriter` | 41 MB (28.0%) | Setup |

**After — Enable command code path now visible:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 13.9 MB (29.4%) | Setup (reduced) |
| 2 | **`cli.setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`** | 10.7 MB (22.8%) | **Measured code** |
| 3 | **`strategy.EnsureSetup`** | 9.2 MB (19.5%) | **Measured code** |
| 4 | **`strategy.EnsureMetadataBranch`** | 8.7 MB (18.5%) | **Measured code** |

### Bottlenecks now visible in commands profiles

2. **`strategy.EnsureMetadataBranch`** (19% mem) — Creating/verifying the

# Benchmark Profile Signal Quality: Before/After Comparison

This document shows how replacing go-git `wt.Add()`/`wt.Commit()` with git CLI
in benchmark setup code improved pprof profile signal, making it possible to
identify actual CLI code bottlenecks.

**Commits:**
- Before: `7ee7d8ba` (benchmark infrastructure with go-git setup)
- After: `e418a1c0` (benchmark setup uses git CLI subprocesses)

**Why this matters:** Go's pprof captures all in-process CPU/memory, including
benchmark setup. `b.StopTimer()` only excludes setup from wall-clock measurement,
not from profiles. By moving setup to git CLI subprocesses, pprof now only sees
the code we're actually benchmarking.

---

## Strategy Package (SaveStep, PostCommit, PrepareCommitMsg, GetRewindPoints)

These are the most performance-critical benchmarks — they measure the hooks and
checkpoint operations that run on every agent interaction and every commit.

### CPU Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total samples** | **18.95s** | **8.50s** (-55%) |

**Before — Top entries are benchmark setup noise:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 54.7% | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 51.6% | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` | 30.9% | Setup + real |
| 4 | `strategy.benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` | 27.3% | Setup |
| 5 | `go-git Worktree.Status` | 26.3% | Setup |

**After — Top entries are actual CLI code paths:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.WriteTemporary`** | 40.7% | **Measured code** |
| 2 | `benchutil.BenchRepo.SeedShadowBranch` | 40.0% | Setup (real checkpoint code) |
| 3 | `go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` | 34.9% | Real (blob writes) |
| 4 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.buildTreeWithChanges`** | 34.2% | **Measured code** |
| 5 | `go-git ObjectWriter.Close` | 23.4% | Real (object persistence) |

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total allocations** | **4,711 MB** | **1,111 MB** (-76%) |

**Before — 78% of allocations are from benchmark setup:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 3,712 MB (78.8%) | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 3,666 MB (77.8%) | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git Worktree.Status` | 2,503 MB (53.1%) | Setup |
| 4 | `go-git Worktree.status` | 2,431 MB (51.6%) | Setup |
| 5 | `strategy.benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` | 2,067 MB (43.9%) | Setup |

**After — Top allocators are actual checkpoint code:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.WriteTemporary`** | 602 MB (54.2%) | **Measured code** |
| 2 | `benchutil.BenchRepo.SeedShadowBranch` | 594 MB (53.4%) | Setup (real checkpoint code) |
| 3 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.buildTreeWithChanges`** | 520 MB (46.8%) | **Measured code** |
| 4 | `go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` | 417 MB (37.6%) | Real (blob writes) |
| 5 | `go-git osfs.BoundOS.abs` | 330 MB (29.7%) | Real (path resolution) |

### Bottlenecks now visible in strategy profiles

With setup noise removed, the profiles reveal actionable optimization targets:

1. **`checkpoint.GitStore.buildTreeWithChanges`** (34% CPU, 47% mem) — Tree surgery
   for each checkpoint. Uses `ApplyTreeChanges` which walks affected subtrees.
2. **`go-git ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject`** (35% CPU, 38% mem) — Writing blobs
   and trees to `.git/objects/`. Each object is zlib-compressed individually.
3. **`go-git osfs.BoundOS.abs` → `SecureJoinVFS`** (30% mem) — Path validation
   on every filesystem operation. go-git calls `filepath-securejoin` per object write.
4. **`go-git ObjectWriter.Close/save`** (23% CPU, 27% mem) — Flushing compressed
   objects to disk with fsync.

---

## Commands Package (Status, Enable)

### CPU Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total samples** | **950ms** | **580ms** (-39%) |

**Before — Setup dominates even this small package:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 45.3% | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 35.8% | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git Worktree.copyFileToStorage` | 24.2% | Setup |

**After — Actual command code visible:**

| Rank | Function | Cum% | Category |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | `os.RemoveAll` | 31.0% | Cleanup (test teardown) |
| 2 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 17.2% | Setup (reduced) |
| 3 | No go-git Worktree entries | — | Eliminated |

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total allocations** | **145.86 MB** | **47.14 MB** (-68%) |

**Before — 83% is setup:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 121 MB (83.1%) | Setup |
| 2 | `go-git Worktree.Add` | 101 MB (69.1%) | Setup |
| 3 | `go-git Worktree.doAddFile` | 63 MB (43.0%) | Setup |
| 4 | `compress/flate.NewWriter` | 41 MB (28.0%) | Setup |

**After — Enable command code path now visible:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | 13.9 MB (29.4%) | Setup (reduced) |
| 2 | **`cli.setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`** | 10.7 MB (22.8%) | **Measured code** |
| 3 | **`strategy.EnsureSetup`** | 9.2 MB (19.5%) | **Measured code** |
| 4 | **`strategy.EnsureMetadataBranch`** | 8.7 MB (18.5%) | **Measured code** |

### Bottlenecks now visible in commands profiles

1. **`setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`** (23% mem) — The enable command's hook
   installation path. Previously invisible under setup noise.
2. **`strategy.EnsureMetadataBranch`** (19% mem) — Creating/verifying the
   `entire/checkpoints/v1` orphan branch. Allocates ~8.7 MB per invocation.

---

## Tree Operations Package (UpdateSubtree, ApplyTreeChanges, WriteTemporary, WriteCommitted)

Tree benchmarks test go-git plumbing operations directly. The setup
(`buildShardedMetadataTree`, `buildFlatFileTree`) also uses go-git, so the
before/after difference is smaller here — both are measuring go-git code.

### CPU Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total samples** | **27.76s** | **24.95s** (-10%) |

Top entries are nearly identical because the benchmarks themselves use go-git:

| Rank | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| 1 | `ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` (60%) | `ObjectStorage.SetEncodedObject` (62%) |
| 2 | `checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent` (31%) | `checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent` (34%) |
| 3 | `buildShardedMetadataTree` (28%) | `buildShardedMetadataTree` (31%) |

The ~10% reduction comes from `NewBenchRepo` no longer using go-git for its
initial commit (only affects `BenchmarkWriteTemporary` and `BenchmarkSeedShadowBranch`).

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total allocations** | **4,493 MB** | **3,698 MB** (-18%) |

**Before — `NewBenchRepo` setup mixed with real benchmark code:**

Top entries are all go-git internals — hard to distinguish setup from measured code.

**After — `NewBenchRepo` reduced, real code more prominent:**

| Rank | Function | Alloc | Category |
|------|----------|-------|----------|
| 1 | **`checkpoint.GitStore.WriteCommitted`** | 1,341 MB (36.3%) | **Measured code** |
| 2 | **`checkpoint.writeStandardCheckpointEntries`** | 1,159 MB (31.3%) | **Measured code** |
| 3 | **`checkpoint.writeSessionToSubdirectory`** | 1,128 MB (30.5%) | **Measured code** |
| 4 | **`checkpoint.writeTranscript`** | 1,088 MB (29.4%) | **Measured code** |
| 5 | **`checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent`** | 1,068 MB (28.9%) | **Measured code** |

### Bottlenecks now visible in tree profiles

1. **`checkpoint.writeTranscript`** (29% mem) — Serializing transcript data to
   git blobs. Largest single allocation source in `WriteCommitted`.
2. **`checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent`** (29% mem) — Creating individual git
   blob objects. Each call allocates zlib writer + buffer.
3. **`SecureJoinVFS`** (29% mem) — Path security validation on every go-git
   filesystem operation. Significant cumulative cost.

---

## Summary

| Package | Profile Type | Before (setup noise) | After (clean signal) | Reduction |
|---------|-------------|---------------------|---------------------|-----------|
| **Strategy** | CPU samples | 18.95s | 8.50s | **-55%** |
| **Strategy** | Memory | 4,711 MB | 1,111 MB | **-76%** |
| **Commands** | CPU samples | 950ms | 580ms | **-39%** |
| **Commands** | Memory | 146 MB | 47 MB | **-68%** |
| **Tree ops** | CPU samples | 27.76s | 24.95s | **-10%** |
| **Tree ops** | Memory | 4,493 MB | 3,698 MB | **-18%** |

The largest improvements are in the **strategy** and **commands** packages where
`NewBenchRepo`'s go-git `wt.Add()` was the dominant allocator. The tree ops package
shows smaller improvement because its benchmarks inherently use go-git plumbing.

**Key insight:** Before the fix, the top 5 pprof entries across all packages were
go-git's `Worktree.Add`, `Worktree.Status`, and `NewBenchRepo` — none of which are
actual CLI code. After the fix, the top entries are `WriteTemporary`,
`buildTreeWithChanges`, `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`, and `EnsureMetadataBranch`
— all real CLI code paths where optimization effort would yield user-visible improvements.

# Benchmark Profile Signal Quality: Before/After Comparison

This document shows how replacing go-git `wt.Add()`/`wt.Commit()` with git CLI
in benchmark setup code improved pprof profile signal, making it possible to
identify actual CLI code bottlenecks.

**Commits:**
- Before: `7ee7d8ba` (benchmark infrastructure with go-git setup)
- After: `e418a1c0` (benchmark setup uses git CLI subprocesses)

**Why this matters:** Go's pprof captures all in-process CPU/memory, including
benchmark setup. `b.StopTimer()` only excludes setup from wall-clock measurement,
not from profiles. By moving setup to git CLI subprocesses, pprof now only sees
the code we're actually benchmarking.

**Profile images:** `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/{before,after}/` contains
per-benchmark CPU and MEM pprof PNGs for side-by-side comparison.

---

## Best Example: EnableCommand (existing benchmark)

This is the most dramatic per-benchmark improvement. Before the fix, the
`BenchmarkEnableCommand` memory profile was dominated by `NewBenchRepo` setup.
After, the actual enable command code path is clearly visible.

**Profile images:**
- `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/EnableCommand_mem.png`
- `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/EnableCommand_mem.png`

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total** | **23.8 KB** profiled | **18.5 KB** profiled |

**Before — `NewBenchRepo` setup obscures the actual command:**

| Rank | Function | % | Category |
|------|----------|---|----------|
| 1 | `BenchmarkEnableCommand.func1` | 45% | Benchmark harness |
| 2 | `cli.setupAgentHooksNonInteractive` | 30% | **Measured code** (hard to see) |
| 3 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | **26%** | **Setup noise** |
| 4 | `compress/flate.NewWriter` | 26% | Setup (zlib for go-git objects) |

**After — Real code path clearly visible:**

| Rank | Function | % | Category |
|------|----------|---|----------|
| 1 | **`cli.setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`** | **37%** | **Measured code** ✓ |
| 2 | `BenchmarkEnableCommand.func1` | 34% | Benchmark harness |
| 3 | `compress/flate.NewWriter` | 32% | Real (metadata branch creation) |
| 4 | **`strategy.EnsureSetup`** | **32%** | **Measured code** ✓ |
| 5 | **`strategy.EnsureMetadataBranch`** | **26%** | **Measured code** ✓ |

`NewBenchRepo` drops from 26% to invisible. `EnsureMetadataBranch` — a real
optimization target — only appears in the after profile.

---

## Per-Benchmark Comparison Index

Each benchmark has before/after CPU and MEM profile PNGs in
`bench-profiles/per-benchmark/{before,after}/`.

### Existing Benchmarks

#### PostCommit (existing) — `strategy` package

Measures the full PostCommit hook: condensation, tree surgery, shadow branch cleanup.

**Profile images:** `PostCommit_cpu.png`, `PostCommit_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 144 MB | 128 MB (-11%) | `PostCommit` 47%, `WriteTemporary` 45% |
| CPU | 9.26s | 9.06s (-2%) | `buildTreeWithChanges`, `SetEncodedObject` |

Before: `benchSetupPostCommitRepo` at 45% (uses `SaveStep` internally — real code).
After: `PostCommit` itself at 47% — setup noise from go-git `wt.Add`/`wt.Commit`
eliminated by git CLI replacement in `benchSetupPostCommitRepo`.

#### PrepareCommitMsg (existing) — `strategy` package

Measures the commit hook: session lookup, content detection, staged file scanning.

**Profile images:** `PrepareCommitMsg_cpu.png`, `PrepareCommitMsg_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 206 MB | 220 MB (+7%) | `benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` 78% |
| CPU | 7.15s | 7.16s (0%) | Unchanged |

**Note:** This benchmark still shows `wt.Add` (29%) in both before and after because
`benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` has its own inline `wt.Add` for staging files —
not yet migrated to git CLI. The `NewBenchRepo` portion was fixed, but the staging
loop remains. This is a candidate for a follow-up fix.

#### GetStagedFiles (existing) — `strategy` package

Measures `git diff --cached --name-only` subprocess call.

**Profile images:** `GetStagedFiles_cpu.png`, `GetStagedFiles_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 75 MB | 74 MB (-2%) | Minimal — mostly subprocess I/O |
| CPU | 2.72s | 2.73s (0%) | `syscall.rawsyscalln` (expected — subprocess wait) |

No significant change — this benchmark already measured a git CLI call with minimal
in-process setup.

#### EnableCommand (existing) — `cli` package

Measures `entire enable --agent claude-code` hook installation path.

**Profile images:** `EnableCommand_cpu.png`, `EnableCommand_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 23.8 KB | 18.5 KB (-22%) | `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive` 37% |
| CPU | 1.21s | 1.41s (+17%) | Subprocess overhead (git CLI init) |

**Best improvement.** See detailed analysis at top of document.

#### StatusCommand (existing) — `cli` package

Measures `entire status` latency vs session count.

**Profile images:** `StatusCommand_cpu.png`, `StatusCommand_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | ~small | ~small | `runStatus`, `session.NewStateStore` |
| CPU | 2.92s | 3.12s (+7%) | `git rev-parse` subprocess calls |

Minimal change — `BenchmarkStatusCommand` setup was already cheap (only
`CreateSessionState` filesystem writes, no go-git `wt.Add`).

#### StatusCommand_NoCache (existing) — `cli` package

Same as StatusCommand but clears git common dir cache each iteration.

**Profile images:** `StatusCommand_NoCache_cpu.png`, `StatusCommand_NoCache_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | ~small | ~small | `session.NewStateStore` |
| CPU | 3.22s | 3.22s (0%) | `git rev-parse` subprocess calls |

No change — same reason as StatusCommand.

#### WriteTemporary (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures shadow branch checkpoint creation (go-git plumbing).

**Profile images:** `WriteTemporary_cpu.png`, `WriteTemporary_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 201 MB | 205 MB (+2%) | `WriteTemporary`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |
| CPU | 3.42s | 3.63s (+6%) | `SetEncodedObject`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |

Minimal change — this benchmark measures go-git plumbing directly.
`NewBenchRepo` setup was a small fraction of the total.

#### WriteCommitted (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures metadata branch checkpoint creation.

**Profile images:** `WriteCommitted_cpu.png`, `WriteCommitted_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 1,542 MB | 1,522 MB (-1%) | `writeTranscript`, `CreateBlobFromContent` |
| CPU | 8.68s | 8.99s (+4%) | `SetEncodedObject` |

Dominated by transcript serialization — setup is negligible.

#### UpdateSubtree (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures tree surgery vs flatten-rebuild for metadata branch updates.

**Profile images:** `UpdateSubtree_cpu.png`, `UpdateSubtree_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 1,611 MB | 1,627 MB (+1%) | `FlattenTree`, `BuildTreeFromEntries` |
| CPU | 13.11s | 13.22s (+1%) | `SetEncodedObject` |

No change — setup (`buildShardedMetadataTree`) uses go-git plumbing directly.

#### ApplyTreeChanges (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures working tree modifications: surgery vs flatten-rebuild.

**Profile images:** `ApplyTreeChanges_cpu.png`, `ApplyTreeChanges_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 395 MB | 385 MB (-2%) | `ApplyTreeChanges`, `FlattenTree` |
| CPU | 3.33s | 3.33s (0%) | `SetEncodedObject` |

No change — setup (`buildFlatFileTree`) uses go-git plumbing directly.

#### NewBenchRepo (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures the benchmark setup helper itself.

**Profile images:** `NewBenchRepo_cpu.png`, `NewBenchRepo_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | ~small | ~small | Before: `wt.Add`; After: `git.PlainOpen` |
| CPU | 1.71s | 1.71s (0%) | Before: in-process go-git; After: subprocess |

This benchmark directly measures the setup helper. Before: go-git `wt.Add` dominates.
After: subprocess calls dominate. The **in-process allocations** drop dramatically,
which is the whole point — pprof no longer sees the setup work.

#### SeedShadowBranch (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures shadow branch seeding with N checkpoints.

**Profile images:** `SeedShadowBranch_cpu.png`, `SeedShadowBranch_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 92 MB | 87 MB (-6%) | `WriteTemporary`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |
| CPU | 3.22s | 2.92s (-9%) | `SetEncodedObject` |

Small improvement — `SeedShadowBranch` calls `NewBenchRepo` internally, so the
git CLI change in `NewBenchRepo` reduces its profile footprint slightly.

### New Benchmarks

#### SaveStep (new) — `strategy` package

Measures per-prompt checkpoint creation to shadow branch. This is the most
frequently called operation — invoked every time an agent tool fires.

**Profile images:** `SaveStep_cpu.png`, `SaveStep_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 304 MB | 307 MB (+1%) | `WriteTemporary` 66%, `buildTreeWithChanges` 59% |
| CPU | 9.07s | 9.69s (+7%) | `SetEncodedObject`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |

Both before and after show the same real code paths because `SaveStep` uses
`b.StopTimer`/`b.StartTimer` with fresh repo per iteration. The `NewBenchRepo`
change is in setup (stopped timer) so per-benchmark profiles are similar.
The benefit shows at the **package level** where other benchmarks' `NewBenchRepo`
calls no longer pollute the aggregate profile.

#### GetRewindPoints (new) — `strategy` package

Measures listing available rewind points from shadow branches. Called when
the user runs `entire rewind`.

**Profile images:** `GetRewindPoints_cpu.png`, `GetRewindPoints_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 502 MB | 487 MB (-3%) | `SeedShadowBranch` 53%, `WriteTemporary` 52% |
| CPU | 6.46s | 6.45s (0%) | `SetEncodedObject`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |

Setup (`SeedShadowBranch`) is the dominant allocator because it creates
many checkpoints. The measured `GetRewindPoints` code is visible at ~20% —
shadow branch traversal and session prompt reading.

---

## Package-Level Aggregate Comparison

The biggest impact is at the **package level** where `NewBenchRepo` from multiple
benchmarks accumulates into massive setup noise in the aggregate profile.

**Profile images:** `bench-profiles/{before,after}/{strategy,commands,tree}_{cpu,mem}.png`

| Package | Profile | Before | After | Reduction |
|---------|---------|--------|-------|-----------|
| **Strategy** | CPU samples | 18.95s | 8.50s | **-55%** |
| **Strategy** | Memory | 4,711 MB | 1,111 MB | **-76%** |
| **Commands** | CPU samples | 950ms | 580ms | **-39%** |
| **Commands** | Memory | 146 MB | 47 MB | **-68%** |
| **Tree ops** | CPU samples | 27.76s | 24.95s | **-10%** |
| **Tree ops** | Memory | 4,493 MB | 3,698 MB | **-18%** |

The strategy package has the largest improvement because it has the most benchmarks
(PostCommit, PrepareCommitMsg, GetStagedFiles, SaveStep, GetRewindPoints) each
creating repos via `NewBenchRepo`. The tree ops package shows less improvement
because its benchmarks inherently measure go-git plumbing operations.

---

## Key Insight

**Before:** The top 5 pprof entries across all packages were go-git's
`Worktree.Add`, `Worktree.Status`, and `NewBenchRepo` — none of which are
actual CLI code.

**After:** The top entries are `WriteTemporary`, `buildTreeWithChanges`,
`setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`, and `EnsureMetadataBranch` — all real CLI
code paths where optimization effort yields user-visible improvements.

For maintainers: the **EnableCommand** memory profile is the clearest example.
Compare `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/EnableCommand_mem.png` with
`bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/EnableCommand_mem.png` — `NewBenchRepo`
drops from 26% to invisible, and `EnsureMetadataBranch` (a real bottleneck
allocating ~8.7 MB per invocation) becomes visible only in the after profile.

# Benchmarking Infrastructure for CLI Hot Path Detection

## Context

Adding benchmarking infrastructure to detect CPU and memory hot paths in CLI commands and hooks, and improving pprof profile signal-to-noise ratio so profiles show actual measured code paths instead of benchmark setup overhead.

## Commits

All changes are already implemented in the working tree. The plan is to split them into 3 commits.

### Commit 1: Add benchmark infrastructure

Extend benchmarking coverage with new benchmarks, mise tasks, and allocation reporting.

**Files to stage**:
- `mise.toml` — `bench` and `bench:profile` tasks
- `cmd/entire/cli/bench_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/bench_enable_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/preparecommitmsg_bench_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/postcommit_bench_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()` only (NOT the git CLI changes)
- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/hook_bench_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/benchutil/parse_tree_bench_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/savestep_bench_test.go` — **new** SaveStep benchmark
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/rewind_bench_test.go` — **new** GetRewindPoints benchmark
- `.gitignore` — `bench-profiles/`

**Problem**: `postcommit_bench_test.go` currently has BOTH `b.ReportAllocs()` AND the git CLI changes mixed together. Need to create a version with only `b.ReportAllocs()` for commit 1, then the full git CLI version for commit 2.

**Approach**: Use `git add -p` to stage only the `b.ReportAllocs()` hunks from `postcommit_bench_test.go`, or temporarily revert the git CLI changes in that file for commit 1, then re-apply for commit 2.

### Commit 2: Reduce pprof noise by replacing go-git setup with git CLI

Replace go-git `wt.Add()`/`wt.Commit()` in benchmark setup with git CLI subprocess calls. This moves setup work out of the Go process, making it invisible to pprof so profiles show actual measured code paths.

**Files to stage**:
- `cmd/entire/cli/benchutil/benchutil.go` — `NewBenchRepo`/`AddAndCommit` use git CLI, `gitCmd`/`refreshRepo` helpers
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/postcommit_bench_test.go` — `benchSetupPostCommitRepo` uses git CLI, `benchGitCmd` helper

### Commit 3: Add reproduction instructions

Add a doc with step-by-step instructions to reproduce before/after benchmark profiles, referencing the commit SHAs from commits 1 and 2.

**File to create**: `docs/benchmarking.md` (or similar)

**Contents**: Instructions using the actual commit SHAs, showing how to:
1. Checkout commit 1, run `mise run bench:profile`, examine the noisy profiles
2. Checkout commit 2, run `mise run bench:profile`, examine the clean profiles
3. Compare the key metrics

```bash
mise run bench:profile

cp -r bench-profiles bench-profiles-before
mise run bench 2>&1 | tee bench-results-before.txt
```

### Step 2: Profile at commit 2 (after pprof fix)

```bash
git checkout <commit-2-sha>
mise run bench:profile
# Save results
cp -r bench-profiles bench-profiles-after
mise run bench 2>&1 | tee bench-results-after.txt
```

### Step 3: Generate summary

Include in the docs:
- `bench-profiles-before/strategy_cpu.png` vs `bench-profiles-after/strategy_cpu.png` — CPU flame graph comparison
- `bench-profiles-before/strategy_mem.png` vs `bench-profiles-after/strategy_mem.png` — memory profile comparison

- `go tool pprof -top` output for both, showing the top entries shifted from setup code to real code paths

The PNG images and bench results text files are for reference only — they go in the docs commit (commit 3) or are shared separately but NOT committed as binary artifacts.

1. After commit 1: `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run bench` — benchmarks pass with alloc reporting
2. After commit 2: `mise run bench:profile` — profiles show real code paths, not setup noise
3. After commit 3: Doc references correct SHAs and includes reproduction steps

   461→---
   462→
   463→## Package-Level Aggregate Comparison
   464→
   465→The biggest impact is at the **package level** where `NewBenchRepo` from multiple
   466→benchmarks accumulates into massive setup noise in the aggregate profile.

   479→The strategy package has the largest improvement because it has the most benchmarks

   488→**Before:** The top 5 pprof entries across all packages were go-git's

   492→**After:** The top entries are `WriteTemporary`, `buildTreeWithChanges`,

# Benchmark Profile Signal Quality: Before/After Comparison

This document shows how replacing go-git `wt.Add()`/`wt.Commit()` with git CLI
in benchmark setup code improved pprof profile signal, making it possible to
identify actual CLI code bottlenecks.

**Commits:**
- Before: `7ee7d8ba` (benchmark infrastructure with go-git setup)
- After: `e418a1c0` (benchmark setup uses git CLI subprocesses)

**Why this matters:** Go's pprof captures all in-process CPU/memory, including
benchmark setup. `b.StopTimer()` only excludes setup from wall-clock measurement,
not from profiles. By moving setup to git CLI subprocesses, pprof now only sees
the code we're actually benchmarking.

**Profile images:** `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/{before,after}/` contains
per-benchmark CPU and MEM pprof PNGs for side-by-side comparison.

---

## How to Reproduce

### Prerequisites

- Go 1.25+, mise, Graphviz (`brew install graphviz` for PNG generation)

### Quick: Run all benchmarks at both commits

```bash
mkdir -p bench-profiles/per-benchmark/{before,after}

# --- BEFORE (go-git setup) ---
git checkout 7ee7d8ba

# Strategy package (existing: PostCommit, PrepareCommitMsg, GetStagedFiles; new: SaveStep, GetRewindPoints)
go test -bench=BenchmarkPostCommit -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/PostCommit_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/PostCommit_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy

go test -bench=BenchmarkPrepareCommitMsg -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/PrepareCommitMsg_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/PrepareCommitMsg_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy

go test -bench=BenchmarkGetStagedFiles -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/GetStagedFiles_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/GetStagedFiles_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy

go test -bench=BenchmarkSaveStep -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/SaveStep_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/SaveStep_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy

go test -bench=BenchmarkGetRewindPoints -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/GetRewindPoints_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/GetRewindPoints_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy

go test -bench=BenchmarkEnableCommand -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/EnableCommand_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/EnableCommand_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli

go test -bench='BenchmarkStatusCommand$' -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \

# Tree operations package (existing: WriteTemporary, WriteCommitted, UpdateSubtree, ApplyTreeChanges, NewBenchRepo, SeedShadowBranch)

  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/WriteTemporary_mem.prof \

  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/ApplyTreeChanges_mem.prof \

go test -bench=BenchmarkNewBenchRepo -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \

go test -bench=BenchmarkPrepareCommitMsg -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \

  ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy

go test -bench=BenchmarkGetStagedFiles -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/GetStagedFiles_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/GetStagedFiles_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy

go test -bench=BenchmarkSaveStep -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/SaveStep_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/SaveStep_mem.prof \

go test -bench=BenchmarkGetRewindPoints -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \

  ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy

# Commands package
go test -bench=BenchmarkEnableCommand -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/EnableCommand_cpu.prof \

go test -bench='BenchmarkStatusCommand$' -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \

# Tree operations package

  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/WriteTemporary_cpu.prof \
```

### Compare a single benchmark

```bash
# Example: EnableCommand memory profile (best improvement)

```

---

## Best Example: EnableCommand (existing benchmark)

This is the most dramatic per-benchmark improvement. Before the fix, the
`BenchmarkEnableCommand` memory profile was dominated by `NewBenchRepo` setup.
After, the actual enable command code path is clearly visible.

**Profile images:**
- `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/EnableCommand_mem.png`
- `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/EnableCommand_mem.png`

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total** | **23.8 KB** profiled | **18.5 KB** profiled |

**Before — `NewBenchRepo` setup obscures the actual command:**

| Rank | Function | % | Category |
|------|----------|---|----------|
| 1 | `BenchmarkEnableCommand.func1` | 45% | Benchmark harness |
| 2 | `cli.setupAgentHooksNonInteractive` | 30% | **Measured code** (hard to see) |
| 3 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | **26%** | **Setup noise** |
| 4 | `compress/flate.NewWriter` | 26% | Setup (zlib for go-git objects) |

**After — Real code path clearly visible:**

| Rank | Function | % | Category |
|------|----------|---|----------|
| 1 | **`cli.setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`** | **37%** | **Measured code** ✓ |
| 2 | `BenchmarkEnableCommand.func1` | 34% | Benchmark harness |
| 3 | `compress/flate.NewWriter` | 32% | Real (metadata branch creation) |
| 4 | **`strategy.EnsureSetup`** | **32%** | **Measured code** ✓ |
| 5 | **`strategy.EnsureMetadataBranch`** | **26%** | **Measured code** ✓ |

`NewBenchRepo` drops from 26% to invisible. `EnsureMetadataBranch` — a real
optimization target — only appears in the after profile.

---

## Per-Benchmark Comparison Index

Each benchmark has before/after CPU and MEM profile PNGs in
`bench-profiles/per-benchmark/{before,after}/`.

### Existing Benchmarks

#### PostCommit (existing) — `strategy` package

Measures the full PostCommit hook: condensation, tree surgery, shadow branch cleanup.

**Profile images:** `PostCommit_cpu.png`, `PostCommit_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 144 MB | 128 MB (-11%) | `PostCommit` 47%, `WriteTemporary` 45% |
| CPU | 9.26s | 9.06s (-2%) | `buildTreeWithChanges`, `SetEncodedObject` |

Before: `benchSetupPostCommitRepo` at 45% (uses `SaveStep` internally — real code).
After: `PostCommit` itself at 47% — setup noise from go-git `wt.Add`/`wt.Commit`
eliminated by git CLI replacement in `benchSetupPostCommitRepo`.

#### PrepareCommitMsg (existing) — `strategy` package

Measures the commit hook: session lookup, content detection, staged file scanning.

**Profile images:** `PrepareCommitMsg_cpu.png`, `PrepareCommitMsg_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 206 MB | 220 MB (+7%) | `benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` 78% |
| CPU | 7.15s | 7.16s (0%) | Unchanged |

**Note:** This benchmark still shows `wt.Add` (29%) in both before and after because
`benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` has its own inline `wt.Add` for staging files —
not yet migrated to git CLI. The `NewBenchRepo` portion was fixed, but the staging
loop remains. This is a candidate for a follow-up fix.

#### GetStagedFiles (existing) — `strategy` package

Measures `git diff --cached --name-only` subprocess call.

**Profile images:** `GetStagedFiles_cpu.png`, `GetStagedFiles_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 75 MB | 74 MB (-2%) | Minimal — mostly subprocess I/O |
| CPU | 2.72s | 2.73s (0%) | `syscall.rawsyscalln` (expected — subprocess wait) |

No significant change — this benchmark already measured a git CLI call with minimal
in-process setup.

#### EnableCommand (existing) — `cli` package

Measures `entire enable --agent claude-code` hook installation path.

**Profile images:** `EnableCommand_cpu.png`, `EnableCommand_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 23.8 KB | 18.5 KB (-22%) | `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive` 37% |
| CPU | 1.21s | 1.41s (+17%) | Subprocess overhead (git CLI init) |

**Best improvement.** See detailed analysis at top of document.

#### StatusCommand (existing) — `cli` package

Measures `entire status` latency vs session count.

**Profile images:** `StatusCommand_cpu.png`, `StatusCommand_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | ~small | ~small | `runStatus`, `session.NewStateStore` |
| CPU | 2.92s | 3.12s (+7%) | `git rev-parse` subprocess calls |

Minimal change — `BenchmarkStatusCommand` setup was already cheap (only
`CreateSessionState` filesystem writes, no go-git `wt.Add`).

#### StatusCommand_NoCache (existing) — `cli` package

Same as StatusCommand but clears git common dir cache each iteration.

**Profile images:** `StatusCommand_NoCache_cpu.png`, `StatusCommand_NoCache_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | ~small | ~small | `session.NewStateStore` |
| CPU | 3.22s | 3.22s (0%) | `git rev-parse` subprocess calls |

No change — same reason as StatusCommand.

#### WriteTemporary (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures shadow branch checkpoint creation (go-git plumbing).

**Profile images:** `WriteTemporary_cpu.png`, `WriteTemporary_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 201 MB | 205 MB (+2%) | `WriteTemporary`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |
| CPU | 3.42s | 3.63s (+6%) | `SetEncodedObject`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |

Minimal change — this benchmark measures go-git plumbing directly.
`NewBenchRepo` setup was a small fraction of the total.

#### WriteCommitted (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures metadata branch checkpoint creation.

**Profile images:** `WriteCommitted_cpu.png`, `WriteCommitted_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 1,542 MB | 1,522 MB (-1%) | `writeTranscript`, `CreateBlobFromContent` |
| CPU | 8.68s | 8.99s (+4%) | `SetEncodedObject` |

Dominated by transcript serialization — setup is negligible.

#### UpdateSubtree (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures tree surgery vs flatten-rebuild for metadata branch updates.

**Profile images:** `UpdateSubtree_cpu.png`, `UpdateSubtree_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 1,611 MB | 1,627 MB (+1%) | `FlattenTree`, `BuildTreeFromEntries` |
| CPU | 13.11s | 13.22s (+1%) | `SetEncodedObject` |

No change — setup (`buildShardedMetadataTree`) uses go-git plumbing directly.

#### ApplyTreeChanges (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures working tree modifications: surgery vs flatten-rebuild.

**Profile images:** `ApplyTreeChanges_cpu.png`, `ApplyTreeChanges_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 395 MB | 385 MB (-2%) | `ApplyTreeChanges`, `FlattenTree` |
| CPU | 3.33s | 3.33s (0%) | `SetEncodedObject` |

No change — setup (`buildFlatFileTree`) uses go-git plumbing directly.

#### NewBenchRepo (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures the benchmark setup helper itself.

**Profile images:** `NewBenchRepo_cpu.png`, `NewBenchRepo_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | ~small | ~small | Before: `wt.Add`; After: `git.PlainOpen` |
| CPU | 1.71s | 1.71s (0%) | Before: in-process go-git; After: subprocess |

This benchmark directly measures the setup helper. Before: go-git `wt.Add` dominates.
After: subprocess calls dominate. The **in-process allocations** drop dramatically,
which is the whole point — pprof no longer sees the setup work.

#### SeedShadowBranch (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures shadow branch seeding with N checkpoints.

**Profile images:** `SeedShadowBranch_cpu.png`, `SeedShadowBranch_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 92 MB | 87 MB (-6%) | `WriteTemporary`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |
| CPU | 3.22s | 2.92s (-9%) | `SetEncodedObject` |

Small improvement — `SeedShadowBranch` calls `NewBenchRepo` internally, so the
git CLI change in `NewBenchRepo` reduces its profile footprint slightly.

### New Benchmarks

#### SaveStep (new) — `strategy` package

Measures per-prompt checkpoint creation to shadow branch. This is the most
frequently called operation — invoked every time an agent tool fires.

**Profile images:** `SaveStep_cpu.png`, `SaveStep_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 304 MB | 307 MB (+1%) | `WriteTemporary` 66%, `buildTreeWithChanges` 59% |
| CPU | 9.07s | 9.69s (+7%) | `SetEncodedObject`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |

Both before and after show the same real code paths because `SaveStep` uses
`b.StopTimer`/`b.StartTimer` with fresh repo per iteration. The `NewBenchRepo`
change is in setup (stopped timer) so per-benchmark profiles are similar.
The benefit shows at the **package level** where other benchmarks' `NewBenchRepo`
calls no longer pollute the aggregate profile.

#### GetRewindPoints (new) — `strategy` package

Measures listing available rewind points from shadow branches. Called when
the user runs `entire rewind`.

**Profile images:** `GetRewindPoints_cpu.png`, `GetRewindPoints_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 502 MB | 487 MB (-3%) | `SeedShadowBranch` 53%, `WriteTemporary` 52% |
| CPU | 6.46s | 6.45s (0%) | `SetEncodedObject`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |

Setup (`SeedShadowBranch`) is the dominant allocator because it creates
many checkpoints. The measured `GetRewindPoints` code is visible at ~20% —
shadow branch traversal and session prompt reading.

---

## Package-Level Aggregate Comparison

The biggest impact is at the **package level** where `NewBenchRepo` from multiple
benchmarks accumulates into massive setup noise in the aggregate profile.

**Profile images:** `bench-profiles/{before,after}/{strategy,commands,tree}_{cpu,mem}.png`

| Package | Profile | Before | After | Reduction |
|---------|---------|--------|-------|-----------|
| **Strategy** | CPU samples | 18.95s | 8.50s | **-55%** |
| **Strategy** | Memory | 4,711 MB | 1,111 MB | **-76%** |
| **Commands** | CPU samples | 950ms | 580ms | **-39%** |
| **Commands** | Memory | 146 MB | 47 MB | **-68%** |
| **Tree ops** | CPU samples | 27.76s | 24.95s | **-10%** |
| **Tree ops** | Memory | 4,493 MB | 3,698 MB | **-18%** |

The strategy package has the largest improvement because it has the most benchmarks
(PostCommit, PrepareCommitMsg, GetStagedFiles, SaveStep, GetRewindPoints) each
creating repos via `NewBenchRepo`. The tree ops package shows less improvement
because its benchmarks inherently measure go-git plumbing operations.

---

## Key Insight

**Before:** The top 5 pprof entries across all packages were go-git's
`Worktree.Add`, `Worktree.Status`, and `NewBenchRepo` — none of which are
actual CLI code.

**After:** The top entries are `WriteTemporary`, `buildTreeWithChanges`,
`setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`, and `EnsureMetadataBranch` — all real CLI
code paths where optimization effort yields user-visible improvements.

For maintainers: the **EnableCommand** memory profile is the clearest example.
Compare `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/EnableCommand_mem.png` with
`bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/EnableCommand_mem.png` — `NewBenchRepo`
drops from 26% to invisible, and `EnsureMetadataBranch` (a real bottleneck
allocating ~8.7 MB per invocation) becomes visible only in the after profile.

# Benchmarking Infrastructure for CLI Hot Path Detection

## Context

Adding benchmarking infrastructure to detect CPU and memory hot paths in CLI commands and hooks, and improving pprof profile signal-to-noise ratio so profiles show actual measured code paths instead of benchmark setup overhead.

## Commits

All changes are already implemented in the working tree. The plan is to split them into 3 commits.

### Commit 1: Add benchmark infrastructure

Extend benchmarking coverage with new benchmarks, mise tasks, and allocation reporting.

**Files to stage**:
- `mise.toml` — `bench` and `bench:profile` tasks
- `cmd/entire/cli/bench_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/bench_enable_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/preparecommitmsg_bench_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/postcommit_bench_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()` only (NOT the git CLI changes)
- `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/hook_bench_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/benchutil/parse_tree_bench_test.go` — `b.ReportAllocs()`
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/savestep_bench_test.go` — **new** SaveStep benchmark
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/rewind_bench_test.go` — **new** GetRewindPoints benchmark
- `.gitignore` — `bench-profiles/`

**Problem**: `postcommit_bench_test.go` currently has BOTH `b.ReportAllocs()` AND the git CLI changes mixed together. Need to create a version with only `b.ReportAllocs()` for commit 1, then the full git CLI version for commit 2.

**Approach**: Use `git add -p` to stage only the `b.ReportAllocs()` hunks from `postcommit_bench_test.go`, or temporarily revert the git CLI changes in that file for commit 1, then re-apply for commit 2.

### Commit 2: Reduce pprof noise by replacing go-git setup with git CLI

Replace go-git `wt.Add()`/`wt.Commit()` in benchmark setup with git CLI subprocess calls. This moves setup work out of the Go process, making it invisible to pprof so profiles show actual measured code paths.

**Files to stage**:
- `cmd/entire/cli/benchutil/benchutil.go` — `NewBenchRepo`/`AddAndCommit` use git CLI, `gitCmd`/`refreshRepo` helpers
- `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/postcommit_bench_test.go` — `benchSetupPostCommitRepo` uses git CLI, `benchGitCmd` helper

### Commit 3: Add reproduction instructions

Add a doc with step-by-step instructions to reproduce before/after benchmark profiles, referencing the commit SHAs from commits 1 and 2.

**File to create**: `docs/benchmarking.md` (or similar)

**Contents**: Instructions using the actual commit SHAs, showing how to:
1. Checkout commit 1, run `mise run bench:profile`, examine the noisy profiles
2. Checkout commit 2, run `mise run bench:profile`, examine the clean profiles
3. Compare the key metrics

## Before/After Evidence (generated but NOT committed)

After creating commits 1 and 2, generate comparison evidence:

### Step 1: Profile at commit 1 (before pprof fix)

```bash
git checkout <commit-1-sha>
mise run bench:profile
# Save results
cp -r bench-profiles bench-profiles-before
mise run bench 2>&1 | tee bench-results-before.txt
```

### Step 2: Profile at commit 2 (after pprof fix)

```bash
git checkout <commit-2-sha>
mise run bench:profile
# Save results
cp -r bench-profiles bench-profiles-after
mise run bench 2>&1 | tee bench-results-after.txt
```

### Step 3: Generate summary

Include in the docs:
- `bench-profiles-before/strategy_cpu.png` vs `bench-profiles-after/strategy_cpu.png` — CPU flame graph comparison
- `bench-profiles-before/strategy_mem.png` vs `bench-profiles-after/strategy_mem.png` — memory profile comparison
- Diff of `bench-results-before.txt` vs `bench-results-after.txt` — showing commit 2 has same/similar wall-clock but cleaner allocation attribution
- `go tool pprof -top` output for both, showing the top entries shifted from setup code to real code paths

### Expected key metrics

| Metric | Commit 1 (before) | Commit 2 (after) | Change |
|--------|-------------------|-------------------|--------|
| Strategy pprof total memory | ~4,764 MB | ~1,095 MB | -77% |
| Strategy pprof total CPU samples | ~18s | ~9s | -50% |
| Top pprof memory entry | `os.lstatNolog` (setup noise) | `WriteTemporary` (real code) | Signal |
| Top pprof CPU entry | `syscall.rawsyscalln` (setup I/O) | `WriteTemporary` (real code) | Signal |
| Benchmark wall-clock times | ~same | ~same | No change |
| Benchmark allocs/op | ~same | ~same | No change |

The PNG images and bench results text files are for reference only — they go in the docs commit (commit 3) or are shared separately but NOT committed as binary artifacts.

## Verification

2. After commit 2: `mise run bench:profile` — profiles show real code paths, not setup noise
3. After commit 3: Doc references correct SHAs and includes reproduction steps

# Benchmark Profile Signal Quality: Before/After Comparison

This document shows how replacing go-git `wt.Add()`/`wt.Commit()` with git CLI
in benchmark setup code improved pprof profile signal, making it possible to
identify actual CLI code bottlenecks.

**Commits:**
- Before: `7ee7d8ba` (benchmark infrastructure with go-git setup)
- After: `e418a1c0` (benchmark setup uses git CLI subprocesses)

**Why this matters:** Go's pprof captures all in-process CPU/memory, including
benchmark setup. `b.StopTimer()` only excludes setup from wall-clock measurement,
not from profiles. By moving setup to git CLI subprocesses, pprof now only sees
the code we're actually benchmarking.

**Prerequisites:** Go 1.25+, mise, Graphviz (`brew install graphviz` for PNG generation).

**Profile images:** `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/{before,after}/` contains
per-benchmark CPU and MEM pprof PNGs for side-by-side comparison.

---

## Best Example: EnableCommand (existing benchmark)

This is the most dramatic per-benchmark improvement. Before the fix, the
`BenchmarkEnableCommand` memory profile was dominated by `NewBenchRepo` setup.
After, the actual enable command code path is clearly visible.

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total** | **23.8 KB** profiled | **18.5 KB** profiled |

**Before — `NewBenchRepo` setup obscures the actual command:**

| Rank | Function | % | Category |
|------|----------|---|----------|
| 1 | `BenchmarkEnableCommand.func1` | 45% | Benchmark harness |
| 2 | `cli.setupAgentHooksNonInteractive` | 30% | **Measured code** (hard to see) |
| 3 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | **26%** | **Setup noise** |

The biggest impact is at the **package level** where `NewBenchRepo` from multiple

| **Commands** | CPU samples | 950ms | 580ms | **-39%** |
| **Commands** | Memory | 146 MB | 47 MB | **-68%** |
| **Tree ops** | CPU samples | 27.76s | 24.95s | **-10%** |
| **Tree ops** | Memory | 4,493 MB | 3,698 MB | **-18%** |

(PostCommit, PrepareCommitMsg, GetStagedFiles, SaveStep, GetRewindPoints) each
creating repos via `NewBenchRepo`. The tree ops package shows less improvement
because its benchmarks inherently measure go-git plumbing operations.

```bash
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/before/strategy_mem.prof \

go test -bench=. -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=10m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/before/commands_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/before/commands_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli
go test -bench=. -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=10m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/before/tree_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/before/tree_mem.prof \

  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/after/strategy_cpu.prof \

  ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy
go test -bench=. -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=10m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/after/commands_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/after/commands_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli

  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/after/tree_cpu.prof \
```

## Key Insight

**Before:** The top 5 pprof entries across all packages were go-git's
`Worktree.Add`, `Worktree.Status`, and `NewBenchRepo` — none of which are
actual CLI code.

**After:** The top entries are `WriteTemporary`, `buildTreeWithChanges`,
`setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`, and `EnsureMetadataBranch` — all real CLI
code paths where optimization effort yields user-visible improvements.

For maintainers: the **EnableCommand** memory profile is the clearest example.
Compare `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/EnableCommand_mem.png` with
`bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/EnableCommand_mem.png` — `NewBenchRepo`
drops from 26% to invisible, and `EnsureMetadataBranch` (a real bottleneck
allocating ~8.7 MB per invocation) becomes visible only in the after profile.

# Benchmark Profile Signal Quality: Before/After Comparison

This document shows how replacing go-git `wt.Add()`/`wt.Commit()` with git CLI
in benchmark setup code improved pprof profile signal, making it possible to
identify actual CLI code bottlenecks.

**Commits:**
- Before: `7ee7d8ba` (benchmark infrastructure with go-git setup)
- After: `e418a1c0` (benchmark setup uses git CLI subprocesses)

**Why this matters:** Go's pprof captures all in-process CPU/memory, including
benchmark setup. `b.StopTimer()` only excludes setup from wall-clock measurement,
not from profiles. By moving setup to git CLI subprocesses, pprof now only sees
the code we're actually benchmarking.

**Prerequisites:** Go 1.25+, mise, Graphviz (`brew install graphviz` for PNG generation).

**Profile images:** `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/{before,after}/` contains
per-benchmark CPU and MEM pprof PNGs for side-by-side comparison.

---

## Best Example: EnableCommand (existing benchmark)

This is the most dramatic per-benchmark improvement. Before the fix, the
`BenchmarkEnableCommand` memory profile was dominated by `NewBenchRepo` setup.
After, the actual enable command code path is clearly visible.

### Memory Profile

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Total** | **23.8 KB** profiled | **18.5 KB** profiled |

**Before — `NewBenchRepo` setup obscures the actual command:**

| Rank | Function | % | Category |
|------|----------|---|----------|
| 1 | `BenchmarkEnableCommand.func1` | 45% | Benchmark harness |
| 2 | `cli.setupAgentHooksNonInteractive` | 30% | **Measured code** (hard to see) |
| 3 | `benchutil.NewBenchRepo` | **26%** | **Setup noise** |
| 4 | `compress/flate.NewWriter` | 26% | Setup (zlib for go-git objects) |

**After — Real code path clearly visible:**

| Rank | Function | % | Category |
|------|----------|---|----------|
| 1 | **`cli.setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`** | **37%** | **Measured code** ✓ |
| 2 | `BenchmarkEnableCommand.func1` | 34% | Benchmark harness |
| 3 | `compress/flate.NewWriter` | 32% | Real (metadata branch creation) |
| 4 | **`strategy.EnsureSetup`** | **32%** | **Measured code** ✓ |
| 5 | **`strategy.EnsureMetadataBranch`** | **26%** | **Measured code** ✓ |

`NewBenchRepo` drops from 26% to invisible. `EnsureMetadataBranch` — a real
optimization target — only appears in the after profile.

<details><summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash

# Before

go test -bench=BenchmarkEnableCommand -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/EnableCommand_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/EnableCommand_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli

# After
git checkout e418a1c0
go test -bench=BenchmarkEnableCommand -benchtime=5x -benchmem -run='^$' -timeout=5m \
  -cpuprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/EnableCommand_cpu.prof \
  -memprofile=bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/EnableCommand_mem.prof \
  ./cmd/entire/cli

# Generate PNGs and compare
```

# Benchmark Profile Signal Quality: Before/After Comparison

This document shows how replacing go-git `wt.Add()`/`wt.Commit()` with git CLI
in benchmark setup code improved pprof profile signal, making it possible to
identify actual CLI code bottlenecks.

**Commits:**
- Before: `7ee7d8ba` (benchmark infrastructure with go-git setup)
- After: `e418a1c0` (benchmark setup uses git CLI subprocesses)

**Why this matters:** Go's pprof captures all in-process CPU/memory, including
benchmark setup. `b.StopTimer()` only excludes setup from wall-clock measurement,
not from profiles. By moving setup to git CLI subprocesses, pprof now only sees
the code we're actually benchmarking.

**Profile images:** `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/{before,after}/` contains
per-benchmark CPU and MEM pprof PNGs for side-by-side comparison.

---

optimization target — only appears in the after profile.

## Per-Benchmark Comparison Index

Each benchmark has before/after CPU and MEM profile PNGs in
`bench-profiles/per-benchmark/{before,after}/`.

Measures the full PostCommit hook: condensation, tree surgery, shadow branch cleanup.

**Profile images:** `PostCommit_cpu.png`, `PostCommit_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 144 MB | 128 MB (-11%) | `PostCommit` 47%, `WriteTemporary` 45% |
| CPU | 9.26s | 9.06s (-2%) | `buildTreeWithChanges`, `SetEncodedObject` |

Before: `benchSetupPostCommitRepo` at 45% (uses `SaveStep` internally — real code).
After: `PostCommit` itself at 47% — setup noise from go-git `wt.Add`/`wt.Commit`
eliminated by git CLI replacement in `benchSetupPostCommitRepo`.

#### PrepareCommitMsg (existing) — `strategy` package

Measures the commit hook: session lookup, content detection, staged file scanning.

**Profile images:** `PrepareCommitMsg_cpu.png`, `PrepareCommitMsg_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 206 MB | 220 MB (+7%) | `benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` 78% |
| CPU | 7.15s | 7.16s (0%) | Unchanged |

**Note:** This benchmark still shows `wt.Add` (29%) in both before and after because
`benchSetupPrepareCommitMsgRepo` has its own inline `wt.Add` for staging files —
not yet migrated to git CLI. The `NewBenchRepo` portion was fixed, but the staging
loop remains. This is a candidate for a follow-up fix.

#### GetStagedFiles (existing) — `strategy` package

Measures `git diff --cached --name-only` subprocess call.

**Profile images:** `GetStagedFiles_cpu.png`, `GetStagedFiles_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 75 MB | 74 MB (-2%) | Minimal — mostly subprocess I/O |
| CPU | 2.72s | 2.73s (0%) | `syscall.rawsyscalln` (expected — subprocess wait) |

No significant change — this benchmark already measured a git CLI call with minimal
in-process setup.

#### EnableCommand (existing) — `cli` package

Measures `entire enable --agent claude-code` hook installation path.

**Profile images:** `EnableCommand_cpu.png`, `EnableCommand_mem.png`

| MEM | 23.8 KB | 18.5 KB (-22%) | `setupAgentHooksNonInteractive` 37% |

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |

Measures the benchmark setup helper itself.

This benchmark directly measures the setup helper. Before: go-git `wt.Add` dominates.
After: subprocess calls dominate. The **in-process allocations** drop dramatically,
which is the whole point — pprof no longer sees the setup work.

#### SeedShadowBranch (existing) — `benchutil` package

Measures shadow branch seeding with N checkpoints.

**Profile images:** `SeedShadowBranch_cpu.png`, `SeedShadowBranch_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|

git CLI change in `NewBenchRepo` reduces its profile footprint slightly.

### New Benchmarks

#### SaveStep (new) — `strategy` package

Measures per-prompt checkpoint creation to shadow branch. This is the most
frequently called operation — invoked every time an agent tool fires.

**Profile images:** `SaveStep_cpu.png`, `SaveStep_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 304 MB | 307 MB (+1%) | `WriteTemporary` 66%, `buildTreeWithChanges` 59% |
| CPU | 9.07s | 9.69s (+7%) | `SetEncodedObject`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |

Both before and after show the same real code paths because `SaveStep` uses
`b.StopTimer`/`b.StartTimer` with fresh repo per iteration. The `NewBenchRepo`
change is in setup (stopped timer) so per-benchmark profiles are similar.
The benefit shows at the **package level** where other benchmarks' `NewBenchRepo`
calls no longer pollute the aggregate profile.

#### GetRewindPoints (new) — `strategy` package

Measures listing available rewind points from shadow branches. Called when
the user runs `entire rewind`.

**Profile images:** `GetRewindPoints_cpu.png`, `GetRewindPoints_mem.png`

| Profile | Before | After | Top entry (after) |
|---------|--------|-------|-------------------|
| MEM | 502 MB | 487 MB (-3%) | `SeedShadowBranch` 53%, `WriteTemporary` 52% |
| CPU | 6.46s | 6.45s (0%) | `SetEncodedObject`, `buildTreeWithChanges` |

Setup (`SeedShadowBranch`) is the dominant allocator because it creates
many checkpoints. The measured `GetRewindPoints` code is visible at ~20% —
shadow branch traversal and session prompt reading.

---

## Package-Level Aggregate Comparison

The biggest impact is at the **package level** where `NewBenchRepo` from multiple
benchmarks accumulates into massive setup noise in the aggregate profile.

**Profile images:** `bench-profiles/{before,after}/{strategy,commands,tree}_{cpu,mem}.png`

| Package | Profile | Before | After | Reduction |
|---------|---------|--------|-------|-----------|
| **Strategy** | CPU samples | 18.95s | 8.50s | **-55%** |
| **Strategy** | Memory | 4,711 MB | 1,111 MB | **-76%** |
| **Commands** | CPU samples | 950ms | 580ms | **-39%** |
| **Commands** | Memory | 146 MB | 47 MB | **-68%** |
| **Tree ops** | CPU samples | 27.76s | 24.95s | **-10%** |
| **Tree ops** | Memory | 4,493 MB | 3,698 MB | **-18%** |

The strategy package has the largest improvement because it has the most benchmarks
(PostCommit, PrepareCommitMsg, GetStagedFiles, SaveStep, GetRewindPoints) each
creating repos via `NewBenchRepo`. The tree ops package shows less improvement
because its benchmarks inherently measure go-git plumbing operations.

---

## Key Insight

**Before:** The top 5 pprof entries across all packages were go-git's
`Worktree.Add`, `Worktree.Status`, and `NewBenchRepo` — none of which are
actual CLI code.

**After:** The top entries are `WriteTemporary`, `buildTreeWithChanges`,
`setupAgentHooksNonInteractive`, and `EnsureMetadataBranch` — all real CLI
code paths where optimization effort yields user-visible improvements.

For maintainers: the **EnableCommand** memory profile is the clearest example.
Compare `bench-profiles/per-benchmark/before/EnableCommand_mem.png` with
`bench-profiles/per-benchmark/after/EnableCommand_mem.png` — `NewBenchRepo`
drops from 26% to invisible, and `EnsureMetadataBranch` (a real bottleneck
allocating ~8.7 MB per invocation) becomes visible only in the after profile.

But `SeedShadowBranch` earlier needs the go-git handle, so the refresh should happen after staging.
